canonical_data: a Lisp workspace per directory holding accepted definitions, managed state, revision history, and checkpoints, recoverable on reopen
strengths: The model works through a real tool loop — develop, execute, preview, rollback, restart resumption — with each call validated and routed before the next model request sees the actual outcome
Every attempt takes a checkpoint first, and caller-supplied goals plus safety invariants accept or reject managed state, so unmet goals keep safe progress while failed checks restore
Revision IDs, history-preserving rollback, evidence-packaging scripts, and architecture diagrams make runs inspectable and recoverable
Accepted definitions persist per workspace and survive fresh processes, and manual Lisp works with no model credentials at all
weaknesses: Chat quality inherits the connected model, and the credential story is bring-your-own OpenAI key or local Underclass configuration
Single maintainer, 63 stars, and days-old pushes: young, thinly adopted, and likely to churn under review
Running it means Nix plus devenv with SBCL and a GPU-less CPU path unaddressed, which narrows who can adopt it
The reference world adapter covers direct defuns and a state table; richer application resources need adapter hooks the reader writes
why_it_matters: A terminal-native coding agent for live Common Lisp images: model-driven development with executable acceptance checks and checkpointed rollback instead of blind code generation.
current_repo_note: Reviewed at HEAD 70146a2 (2026-10-12); the single LICENSE file is the canonical MIT text. README claims verified against the tree: controller tool loop, checkpoint engine, Lisp and Python test suites, and fourteen design ADRs.
